title: Improving the Performance of Grid Connected Wind Generator with a Pi Control Scheme Based on the Metaheuristic Golden Eagle Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Wind power installations are globally established thoroughly, resulting in significant electrical power penetration into power grids. Consequently, tremendous efforts are expended to improvise the performance of the grid-connected Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator driven by a Variable-Speed Wind Turbine (PMSG-VSWT). In this work, a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller based on the golden eagle optimization technique is employed to enhance the grid-connected PMSG-VSWT dynamics and transient stability. The integration of the square error criterion is utilised as a fitness function in the optimization process, which is processed using the simulation-based optimization technique. The proposed control technique&apos;s efficacy is compared to various optimal PI controllers under symmetrical and unsymmetrical fault conditions. This study employs measured real time events collected at the Coimbatore wind farm in Tamil Nadu (India) to produce realistic results and aid in the pursuit of higher performance. The wind farm modelling and simulation are processed using the DIgSILENT power factory/MATLAB Simulink environment and are utilized to test the proposed control approach’s achievability. This study demonstrates that the optimization method improves the wind farm&apos;s performance when compared to observed events and other techniques.
